title: Unsupported Operation Exception querying Frozen Tier data
body: I am running Elasticsearch 8.12.0 on Elastic Cloud with bundled Java. My ILM policy keeps data hot for 10 days and frozen for 80 days. A search across the data stream returns partial results, while bounding it by date to hot data produces no errors. The query filters on keyword customer_id and IP ip_address fields, then sorts descending by the keyword request_id field. The response reports 114 total shards, 92 successful and 22 failed; the failures are partial frozen-tier indices with unsupported_operation_exception. The node log reports a TransportSearchAction shard failure. It looks like the exception may be coming from RewriteCachingDirectoryReader, although I am not sure that code applies because my query is not itself a date-range query.

symptoms_visible: My unbounded data-stream search returns partial results: 22 frozen-tier shards fail with unsupported_operation_exception, while a date range restricted to hot data produces no errors.
N0.label: N0 frozen-tier partial search failures reported

symptoms_visible: The query succeeds without the sort, but with the request_id sort it quickly returns failures for frozen-tier data.
N1.label: N1 failure isolated to keyword sort

symptoms_visible: The search succeeds when @timestamp is the primary sort and request_id is secondary, but fails when request_id is the primary sort.
All indices in my cluster were created on Elasticsearch 8.11.4 or 8.12.0.
N2.label: N2 primary-sort behavior and index origin established

symptoms_visible: I can work around this case, but I would prefer to paginate consistently on request_id for both hot and frozen data.
N3.label: N3 pagination requirement and temporary workaround clarified

symptoms_visible: I have not tested a build containing the fix; the last behavior I confirmed is that removing request_id as the primary sort avoids the frozen-shard failures.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix proposed but not reporter-verified

question_patterns: Does the same query succeed if you remove the sort?
Can you rerun the search without its sort clause and report whether the frozen shards still fail?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, without the sort the query succeeds. With the sort, it executes quickly and fails for the frozen-tier data.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same frozen shards fail with unsupported_operation_exception even when I remove the sort.
Removing the sort succeeds but takes somewhat longer than the failing sorted request.

question_patterns: What mapping does request_id have on one of the affected partial indices?
Can you check _mapping on a failing frozen index and confirm the request_id field type?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: GET _mapping on one of the partial indices shows request_id as type keyword.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On the affected partial indices, request_id is mapped as a date rather than a keyword.

question_patterns: Did this same query and sort work against frozen data before 8.12?
Is this known to be a new failure in 8.12?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not sure. This is a relatively new cluster, and when I was running 8.11 I did not yet have any data in the frozen tier.

edges.comment: Thread c4-c6, reporter's cluster: participant2 asks whether removing the sort works, verifies the field mapping, and asks about prior versions; the reporter supplies the test results and history.

question_patterns: What happens if you make @timestamp the primary sort and request_id the secondary sort?
Can you test the two fields with @timestamp first and report whether the frozen search succeeds?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The query succeeds when I sort by @timestamp descending first and request_id descending second.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It still fails with the same frozen-shard exception when @timestamp is first.

question_patterns: Does swapping those sort fields so request_id is first change the result?
Please test request_id as the primary sort with @timestamp second.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not work when I swap the order and put request_id first, then @timestamp.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails in the same way with request_id first even if I reverse the secondary timestamp order.

question_patterns: Could these indices have been frozen using the old 7.x frozen-index feature?
Which Elasticsearch versions created the indices in this cluster?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: All indices in my cluster were created while running 8.11.4 or 8.12.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: These indices were created and frozen on 7.x before the cluster was upgraded.

edges.comment: Thread c11 and c13-c19, reporter's cluster: the reporter supplies both sort-order outcomes and confirms the indices are native 8.x indices, rejecting the old FreezeIndexAction/unfreeze explanation. Maintainers then recognize that partially mounted searchable snapshots use the relevant FrozenEngine.

question_patterns: What does request_id look like in your application?
Is request_id an opaque keyword, or does it contain sortable time information?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Our request_id used for pagination looks like a Unix timestamp followed by an ID, for example 1706869987264.p2nMNE.

question_patterns: Do you specifically need request_id to remain the primary sort?
Could your API paginate with @timestamp as its primary sort instead?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We store @timestamp too, but we would prefer to paginate on request_id for API consistency and use the same ordering for hot and frozen data.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: We do not need request_id ordering and can permanently remove that sort.

question_patterns: Do the real application queries include a time range?
Are these searches normally bounded by @timestamp?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, in our use case we also filter on date ranges in all queries.

question_patterns: Can you use the working sort order as a temporary workaround?
Are you blocked, or can you temporarily avoid request_id as the primary sort?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We can work around it in this circumstance, although we would still like to sort by the keyword consistently across hot and frozen data.

edges.comment: Thread c10 and c20-c23, reporter's deployment: the reporter explains the request_id format, pagination requirement, normal date filtering, and ability to use a temporary workaround. The discussion of pre_filter_shard_size is not encoded as valid evidence because participant3 later explicitly retracts that recommendation in c25.

solution.intent: Fix the can-match shard-skipping path so an exception while obtaining primary keyword-sort statistics on a partially mounted frozen searchable snapshot falls back to executing the query normally instead of failing the shard.
solution.concrete_example: The keyword primary sort reaches the can-match optimization on partially mounted frozen shards, where the reader cannot provide the requested terms statistics. That limitation must not become a shard failure: catch the exception and fall back to normal query execution without shard skipping. Until a build with that change is available, remove the keyword primary sort or use the confirmed @timestamp-first ordering. A maintainer opened a PR implementing the fallback, but the reporter did not retest a build containing it.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established only the observable sort-dependent behavior and native 8.x index history. Maintainers determined that partially mounted searchable snapshots use the FrozenEngine, that the can-match optimization requests unsupported keyword terms statistics for the primary sort, and that any such exception must trigger normal query execution rather than a shard failure. The earlier pre_filter_shard_size suggestion was explicitly withdrawn.

edges.comment: Final accepted diagnosis from c17-c19 and especially c25-c26: this is not an old-style frozen-index/unfreeze problem and not a legitimate permanent limitation. The shard-skipping optimization must safely fall back. A fix PR was opened and thanked by the reporter, but no affected-user build verification or shipped-fix confirmation appears in the thread, so the terminal state remains unverified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: the can-match shard-skipping optimization tries to obtain statistics for a primary keyword sort on partially mounted frozen searchable snapshots, and the resulting unsupported operation is incorrectly surfaced as shard failures instead of causing normal query execution.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected behavior: removing the sort succeeds, request_id is a keyword, @timestamp-first succeeds, and request_id-first fails.
Must propose the fallback fix: exceptions in the can-match optimization must execute the query without shard skipping rather than return partial results.
Must not recommend POST /_all/_unfreeze as the resolution because all affected indices were created on 8.11.4 or 8.12.0, not by the removed 7.x frozen-index API.

Must not present pre_filter_shard_size as a working solution; the maintainer explicitly withdrew that advice. Removing the keyword primary sort or putting @timestamp first is only a temporary workaround.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the fallback fix and must not declare the issue resolved on the reporter's system because no such retest occurred in the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically experienced Elasticsearch operator who can inspect mappings, compare sort variants, read source code, and reason about ILM tiers, searchable indices, pagination, and query costs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, courteous, and evidence-driven; provides exact queries and mappings, runs focused comparison tests, asks practical follow-up questions, and clearly distinguishes preferences from temporary workarounds.
